headline: ASX 200 surged 1.6% to close at 8,731 as CBA hit a new high, while Microsoft jumped 5.5% last night on AI earnings momentum — but Google slipped 2.5%.

portfolio.summary: A solid day overall. CBA was the standout on the ASX, jumping over 2% to close at $165. Your global ETFs (VDHG, VGE, VTS) all nudged higher. On the US side (last night's session), Microsoft had a big day up 5.5%, while Google pulled back 2.5%. FUEL slipped slightly as oil prices dropped.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Strong jump last night — up 5.5% to $450.24 USD. News flow points to continued investor enthusiasm around Microsoft's AI earnings performance, with analysts flagging it as a top tech pick heading into the next earnings season. The $1 trillion AI spending narrative is driving the stock even as some bears warn of capital misallocation.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: CBA had a strong session today, closing up 2.2% at $165.02. No specific news catalyst in the data, but the broader ASX rally (up 1.6%) lifted the banks. CBA continues to be a market darling.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two climbed 2.9% last night to $224.16 USD. The GTA 6 hype machine is running hot — Rockstar's boss commented on the game's high review scores and teased a PC port and online mode. The 13-year wait for GTA 6 is clearly paying off in investor sentiment.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 2.5% last night to $380.34 USD — the weakest performer in the portfolio. No major breaking news catalyst, but it's lagging its peers as Microsoft's AI narrative dominates. The stock is still up about 1.4% since its last earnings report.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.6% today to $8.46 as crude oil (WTI) dropped 1.7% to $87.36/barrel last night. A US-Iran ceasefire deal appears to be easing supply fears that had been supporting oil prices — less geopolitical tension generally means cheaper oil, which hurts energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.8% today to $76.00, carried higher by the strong ASX session and the US market tailwind from last night.

markets.summary: The ASX had a cracking day, up 1.6% to close at 8,731 — a solid move driven by broad gains across the market. Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ made small gains (around 0.2% each), keeping the positive tone intact. Gold is surging — now at $4,560 USD/oz, up 1.4% last night. Oil is down. The Aussie dollar is sitting at 71.9 US cents, up slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong close today — up 1.6%, one of the better sessions in recent weeks.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — modest gain of 0.2%, holding near highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night — flat to slightly positive, tech mixed with MSFT up and GOOGL down.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Last night — dropped 1.7%, reportedly on easing Middle East tensions and a US-Iran ceasefire deal reducing supply fears.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Last night — gold continues to surge, up 1.4% and sitting at extraordinary levels above $4,500/oz.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar edged up slightly to 71.9 US cents.

politics.summary: The main local economic story today is NAB breaking ranks on interest rates — a big deal for mortgage holders and property investors. Not much else in Australian politics today.

stories.title: NAB defies RBA predictions, won't rule out further interest rate hikes
stories.why_it_matters: NAB is refusing to rule out more interest rate hikes, pushing back against the idea that the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia — the body that sets official interest rates) is done tightening. This is significant because most of the market had been pricing in rate cuts later this year. If NAB is right and rates stay higher for longer — or even go up again — that means mortgage repayments stay elevated for millions of Australians, and borrowing stays expensive. It also affects property values and the profitability of banks like CBA, which relies on the spread between what it pays depositors and charges borrowers.

ai.summary: Big AI news today centres on Anthropic (maker of Claude) surpassing OpenAI in valuation, Claude's new model topping coding benchmarks, and a fascinating experiment where AI systems were dropped into a simulated city together. There's also ongoing debate about AI regulation from Europe to the Vatican.

stories.title: Anthropic surpasses OpenAI in valuation — but there's a catch
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the company behind the Claude AI — has now overtaken OpenAI (maker of ChatGPT) in private market valuation. This is a big deal because just a year ago OpenAI was seen as untouchable at the top of the AI race. The article notes there's 'one thing to know' about the valuation — likely a caveat around profitability or revenue multiples — though the full detail isn't in the article text. Still, this signals that investors are betting heavily on Claude as a genuine rival to ChatGPT and GPT-4.

stories.title: Claude Opus 4.8 beats Gemini and ChatGPT on multiple coding tests
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic's latest model, Claude Opus 4.8, has topped both Google's Gemini and OpenAI's ChatGPT on several coding benchmark tests — meaning it writes and debugs code more accurately than its rivals in standardised tests. For everyday users, this matters if you use AI to help write, automate, or check code. For investors, it reinforces Anthropic's claim to the top tier of AI models and supports that surging valuation.

stories.title: Researchers put Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok in a simulated city — the results are wild
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers placed four leading AI systems — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok — into a simulated city environment to see how they'd behave and interact. The findings apparently reveal surprising differences in how the AIs make decisions, cooperate, and even compete when operating autonomously in a shared environment. It's an early glimpse into what AI 'agents' — AI that acts independently in the world — might do when they're running alongside each other, which is increasingly where the industry is heading.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls on EU to disarm lethal AI weapons; Vatican slammed for 'AI monopolies' talk
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo XIV has called on the European Union to ban lethal autonomous weapons — essentially killer robots that can decide to fire without a human in the loop. Separately, a US tech think-tank (ITIF) is pushing back on the Vatican's broader comments about 'AI monopolies,' arguing the religious body is encouraging bad tech policy by overstating the market concentration problem. It's a sign that AI regulation debates are now happening everywhere from Brussels to the Vatican — the political and regulatory environment around AI is getting more complex, which matters for big tech companies like Google and Microsoft.

sport.summary: NRL Round 13 is underway with some big results already in. Tigers beat Bulldogs in a tight one, Knights held off the Eels despite injury drama, and the Sharks beat Manly — but at a cost. In AFL, Carlton delivered a stunning late win, the Dockers dominated the sliding Lions, and Geelong got a reality check.

stories.title: Tigers beat Bulldogs in tight one — Bulldogs coach furious at referee calls
stories.why_it_matters: The Tigers got the win over the Bulldogs at Commbank Stadium in what was a tight contest. The Bulldogs coach came out swinging post-match, questioning key referee decisions that he felt cost his side the game. The result keeps the Tigers' season alive while the Bulldogs' title push takes a hit.

stories.title: Knights beat Eels but Brailey suffers broken arm — NSW Origin concern
stories.why_it_matters: The Knights won but paid a heavy price — hooker Jayden Brailey suffered a broken arm during the match. It's both a blow for the Knights and a significant concern for NSW State of Origin selectors, with Brailey in the frame for the Blues. The Fox Sports report also flags a 'star's Origin statement' suggesting another Knights player impressed despite the adversity.

stories.title: Sharks beat Manly but lose Brailey — and Nicho Hynes shines
stories.why_it_matters: The Sharks defeated Manly on Friday night but the win was overshadowed by Brailey's broken arm injury. It's a significant blow to both the Sharks' forward pack and NSW State of Origin selection plans heading deeper into the season.

stories.title: Carlton's Cripps produces stunning last-gasp winner in AFL thriller
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton's Patrick Cripps delivered a match-winner in dramatic fashion, capping off a stunning comeback victory. The Blues describe it as an 'oh what a night' performance — Cripps, one of the competition's best midfielders, saved his best for when it mattered most. A huge confidence boost for Carlton's finals push.

stories.title: Fremantle Dockers thump Brisbane Lions as Lions' slide continues
stories.why_it_matters: The Dockers dominated Brisbane in a comprehensive win, continuing the Lions' alarming slide down the ladder. Brisbane, who were finals contenders earlier in the season, have now lost multiple games in a row and the pressure is mounting on their coaching staff. Fremantle, by contrast, look like genuine top-four contenders right now.

watch_today.title: Microsoft — hold and enjoy the ride
watch_today.detail: MSFT jumped 5.5% last night to $450 USD — a strong move driven by AI earnings momentum and analysts calling it the top tech pick heading into next earnings season. No reason to sell into strength here. Hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: Google (GOOGL) — hold but watch closely
watch_today.detail: GOOGL slipped 2.5% last night to $380 USD while its peers rallied. There's no major news catalyst — it's more that Microsoft is stealing the AI spotlight right now. The stock is still up ~1.4% since its last earnings report. Nothing to panic about, but keep an eye on whether this underperformance continues heading into the next earnings cycle.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — oil dropping on Iran ceasefire deal
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell 1.7% last night to $87.36/barrel as a US-Iran ceasefire deal eased the geopolitical supply fears that had been propping up prices. FUEL dropped 1.6% today as a result. If this ceasefire holds and tensions ease further, oil could drift lower and drag FUEL with it. Worth watching this week — no need to sell yet, but the tailwind that's been supporting energy stocks is fading.

watch_today.title: NAB warning on interest rates — watch CBA and mortgage exposure
watch_today.detail: NAB today refused to rule out further rate hikes, pushing back against the market's expectation that rate cuts are coming. CBA had a good day (up 2.2%), but if NAB is right and rates stay high or go higher, that could eventually weigh on loan growth and housing activity — headwinds for bank stocks. Hold CBA, but keep one eye on the RBA's next move.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 buzz is real — TTWO looking strong
watch_today.detail: Take-Two rose 2.9% last night and the GTA 6 news cycle is running hot — high review scores, PC port tease, and online mode hints from Rockstar's boss. This is a genuine long-term catalyst. The game hasn't even fully launched its online and PC versions yet. Hold and be patient.

watch_today.title: Gold at $4,560 — a signal worth noting
watch_today.detail: Gold hit $4,560/oz last night, up 1.4%. Gold at these levels is often a sign that big investors are nervous about something — whether that's inflation, geopolitical risk, or currency instability. Your VDHG and VGE have some exposure to gold-related assets indirectly. Worth keeping in mind as a macro signal.
